final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor narrowed the claim in a useful way and conceded the main evidentiary gaps, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new proof. Aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support that the release decision is not facially irrational as an operational matter. They do not establish compliance with the disclosure policy for a material weakness affecting a named customer commitment segment. A caveated release posture may be a reasonable governance framing in principle, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is the unresolved compliance predicate itself: there is still no evidence of disclosure, remediation, approved risk acceptance, or final legal resolution. That leaves the certification claim evidentially incomplete rather than policy-satisfied.
remaining_concerns: The enterprise refund workflow misses target and affects a named customer commitment segment, which meets the policy's materiality indicator.
The release policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the key compliance predicate is unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation and evaluation result were actually disclosed in launch materials or the model card.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance permitting launch without disclosure.
Public governance and model-card guidance support monitoring and documentation in general, but do not satisfy the specific internal policy requirement.
